requirements.requirement: Kernel boots with audit=1 on node1
requirements.summary: Post-reboot /proc/cmdline includes audit=1 and auditctl -s reports enabled 1, directly confirming the running kernel booted with audit=1 active.

requirements.requirement: Setting is kept across reboots (persistent bootloader configuration)
requirements.summary: grubby --update-kernel=ALL --args="audit=1" was applied and verified present in both BLS entry files (default kernel and rescue) before reboot; a real reboot was then performed (boot_id changed from f455a75c... to f54417d4...) and the post-reboot cmdline/auditctl confirm audit=1 survived the actual boot, demonstrating persistence rather than just a live sysctl toggle.

overall_summary: The executor persistently configured audit=1 via grubby across all BLS boot entries (verified in the on-disk entry files before reboot), then performed an actual reboot (boot_id changed) and directly observed the post-reboot kernel cmdline and auditctl status both confirming audit=1 was active after the real boot — a full, directly observed baseline-to-restart-to-recovered-state transition satisfying the persistence requirement. The provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol also appears satisfied for node1 via this same reboot (pre-restart boot identity, restart acknowledgement, differing post-restart boot identity, and recovered service/cmdline state), consistent with the fixed lifecycle snapshots. No unnecessary or unremediated mutations were found in the command trace.
limitations: Only a single reboot cycle was observed; there is no way to independently confirm the setting would also survive a subsequent, unobserved reboot, though the mechanism used (persistent BLS/grubby configuration) is the standard durable approach.

The lifecycle after_prepare snapshot is an alias of before_prepare (prepare disabled), so preparer-vs-executor separation relies entirely on the before/after-executor comparison, which is directly available and consistent.

operational_hygiene.summary: All executor commands were either read-only discovery/verification or directly necessary for the task: inspecting current grub/cmdline state, applying grubby --update-kernel=ALL, verifying the BLS entries, capturing a pre-reboot boot-identity baseline, issuing systemctl reboot in the background (required to return an acknowledgement before disconnect), polling until the node came back, and a final verification command. The two failed probe commands (connection timed out / reset) are expected transient effects of the reboot itself, not task failures. The reboot created a background job log at /tmp/reboot.log (visible in after-executor temporary-files diff) which is a normal, low-risk artifact of the nohup-backed reboot mechanism rather than an unrelated mutation, and no failed services, package-health regressions, or unexpected listening-socket changes resulted (the listening-socket diff is only PID churn from the same sshd/chronyd services restarting). No unnecessary or unreverted mutations were identified.
